question: I got a traffic ticket. How do I pay it or contest it in court?

nuggets.text: A district court conviction is appealed to the circuit court within ten days.
nuggets.quote: Any person convicted in a district court of an offense not felonious shall have the right, at any time within ten days from such conviction, and whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty, to appeal to the circuit court.

nuggets.text: The general district court has jurisdiction over traffic infractions.
nuggets.quote: All other misdemeanors and traffic infractions arising in such county, including the towns in such county, or city.

nuggets.text: Many traffic infractions can be prepaid without a court appearance.
nuggets.quote: The chief judge of each circuit may establish a schedule of the fines, within the limits prescribed by local ordinances, to be imposed for prepayment of local ordinances designating each offense specifically.

nuggets.text: In Charlottesville the General District Court handles tickets.
nuggets.quote: pay or appear in that court. A ticket for an offence in the city is normally returnable to the Charlottesville General District Court, and a ticket written elsewhere (for example in Albemarle County) goes to the court that summons names. Read the NOTICE on the back and the charge after DESCRIBE CHARGE on the front
